bullets: The assistant now explains how to recover cloud coding sessions that run out of space by opening the same chat in the desktop app.
The assistant now tells you clearly if a chat session has ended when you ask it to clean up a long conversation.
The assistant now recognizes made-up tool names and fixes minor formatting mistakes to ensure commands are understood correctly.
Freebuff is removing GPT-6 Luna and GLM 5.3 Flash in two steps starting November 6, 2026.
Windows users who agree to ad-supported tasks now see a consent message instead of a refusal.
The assistant now uses a new service for web searches that supports multiple keywords and specific extraction goals.
The assistant now stops tasks sooner if it keeps making slightly different failed edits to the same files.
The web version of the assistant can now restart chats that stop due to too many background programs, up to three times a day.
The assistant no longer automatically archives old chat sessions by default.
Cloud session limit messages now include specific details about how much space or memory was in use.
The assistant now translates errors from Codex and Claude Code tools into clear guidance on what went wrong.
The system now supports cloud assistants running sponsored tasks directly on your computer.
The assistant now automatically retries requests if the AI model becomes silent for five minutes before answering.
A new message explains why a chat cannot continue on a more expensive model for free tier users.
The shared rules for cloud chats now support rolling back to previous points in conversation history.
The internal test suite now uses the same level of thinking effort for all AI models to ensure fair scoring.
The model selection screen now shows a single recommended option when the slider only changes thinking effort.
The desktop application now has the internal setup to open projects in tools like code editors and terminals.
The system now tracks when first-time users see the welcome screen in the desktop app.
The shared data rules for cloud chats now include a flag indicating when service limits are reached.
The shared error messages for cloud services now standardize how expired scheduled tasks are reported.
The shared rules for cloud chat history now define a standard label for untitled conversations.
The coding assistant's instructions now include a placeholder for notes about missing browser tools in the cloud.
The shared rules for cloud chats now define a new message for when a scheduled task fails to start.
